explanation:
### How it works

A subarray ending at i has sum k when an earlier prefix equals currentPrefix - k. Store the earliest index for each prefix, which maximizes the length of any later matching subarray. A zero prefix at index -1 allows subarrays starting at zero.

### Steps

1. Initialize prefix zero at index -1.
2. Update the prefix and look for prefix - k.
3. Update the maximum length and store a prefix only on its first occurrence.

### Complexity

- Time: O(n) expected with hashing.
- Space: O(n).

### Things to watch for

- Do not replace the earliest index for a repeated prefix.
- Negative values make a simple sliding window unsuitable.
- Seed the zero prefix before reading the array.
